model: c in {0,1,2}^22, sum(c)<=11; labels are canonical target slots 0..21; unassigned candidates allowed
block_order: b ascending, then a ascending, a+2*b<=11
within_block_order: mask2 numerically ascending; mask1 numerically ascending among a-bit masks disjoint from mask2; code=mask1|(mask2<<22)

steps: For each of 42 type blocks (a,b), enumerate every b-bit mask2 on 22 canonical target slots in strictly increasing numeric order.
For each mask2, enumerate every a-bit mask1 in its complement in strictly increasing numeric order.
Write code=mask1|(mask2<<22) as exactly 8 little-endian bytes, validating mask ranges, disjointness, and bit counts.
Compress each complete type block as one gzip member: level 1, mtime 0, empty filename header; concatenate the 42 members in block order.

Compare raw SHA, type-block raw SHA, counts and ordering against the published metadata. Gzip byte equality also depends on the deflate implementation; historical gzip SHA identifies the original saved payload.
Invoke the public audit.py with --enumeration-file PATH to independently read and verify every saved record.
regeneration.historical_gzip_reproducibility: same input bytes, gzip member policy, and compatible deflate implementation required
